item.title: daemon hook runner: DaemonHookRunner over spawn_until/spawn_with_deadline with group kill guard and concurrency limit, fixed environment, budgets, spawn-site test

results.statement: An active hook replaces the atm task subcommand call: atm runs the hook first, parses its JSON reply, and the subcommand's own logic runs only when the reply is pass-through, or when every hook in the chain replies not-applicable.
results.quote: so the hooks replace the call. the hooks should return json which is processed by atm. We should be able to replace quite a few of (perhaps all) atm task subcommands.
results.context: atm-core #1873 comment 2026-10-18T22:54Z (Rand, round 1, reply to the seven-point hook proposal)
results.deterministic_check: a test registers a task.assign hook whose reply is {"result": "refused", "message": "m"} and asserts the task ledger is unchanged and the command fails with ATM_HOOK_REFUSED carrying m

criteria.no: The item touches none of the three: it is about something else, such as cron schedule storage or startup, the TUI, documentation, or a command other than atm task, and it does not mention an atm task subcommand's request handling, the hook runner, or a hook reply.
criteria.unclear: The item text is too vague to tell whether it touches an atm task subcommand's request handling, the hook runner, or a hook reply.
criteria.yes: The item plans or changes the request handling of an atm task subcommand, the hook runner, or the handling of a hook's reply, including adding a hook to an atm task subcommand or describing how such a subcommand behaves with or without a hook.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` plan or change one of these three things: (1) how an `atm task` subcommand (assign, start, close, move, list, events) handles a request, (2) the component that runs a registered hook, or (3) how atm handles a hook's reply? Judge only whether the item touches one of these three; do not judge whether the item follows `anchor.statement`.

criteria.no: The item does not plan this: it is silent about hook order and reply handling, names hooks only as a topic, covers only the hook runner or the no-hook case, or runs the normal logic before the hook or for a reply that is not pass-through.
criteria.unclear: The item refers to the hook taking over the call but it cannot be determined whether the hook runs first or whether only a pass-through reply lets the normal logic run.
criteria.yes: The item says atm runs the hook first, reads its JSON reply, and continues into the normal subcommand logic only when the reply is pass-through.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` plan for an active hook to take over the atm task subcommand call, so that atm runs the hook first, reads its JSON reply, and continues into the subcommand's normal logic only on a pass-through reply? A refusal reply or a list of replacement commands in place of the normal logic fits this plan. Judge presence of this plan only, not conflict.

criteria.no: The item lets the hook decide as the statement requires, or does not discuss hook order or replies at all.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be determined from the item whether the own logic or the hook's reply is in charge.
criteria.yes: The item keeps the own logic in charge in one of these ways: it runs before the hook, the hook only receives the result afterwards, the reply is not used to decide, or the own logic runs for a reply other than pass-through.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` keep the atm task subcommand's own logic in charge when a hook is active, contrary to `anchor.statement`? That is the case when the own logic runs before the hook, when the hook only receives the result afterwards, when the hook's reply is not used to decide, or when the own logic still runs for a reply other than pass-through. An item that does not discuss hook order or replies does not conflict. Judge conflict only.

A generic mention of hooks, of JSON on stdin, or of a request, without both the shared shape and all three caller fields, does not count. Judge presence only; do not judge conflict.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item rules out the directive; the item may be silent or incomplete about the request.
criteria.unclear: The item says something about the hook request that might or might not exclude the shared shape or the caller information.

contradicted.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires every hooked command to pass its hook one request with the same top-level shape, holding the full subcommand request and the caller's identity, team and host. Does `item.text` state a design that rules this out? Conflicts include: different request types or top-level fields for different commands or for cron ticks; ad-hoc JSON per subcommand; the caller's identity, team or host kept out of the request (for example passed only as environment variables) or stated as not sent. An item that does not mention the request, or describes it incompletely without excluding anything, is not a conflict. Different contents inside the request field for different commands are not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` describe work on how atm handles a hook's reply for a hooked `atm task` subcommand (assign, start, close, move, list, events)? This includes parsing the hook's JSON reply, deciding what atm does for a handled, pass-through, not-applicable or refused reply, and the path by which atm continues to the subcommand's own logic after its hook returns. Judge subject matter only, not whether the item handles the reply correctly.

criteria.no: The item does not state that behaviour: it is silent about the pass-through reply, only names the case or a branch without saying what happens, covers only other replies such as refusals or action lists, or describes a different outcome for that reply.
criteria.unclear: The item describes what happens on a pass-through reply in words that may or may not mean the normal logic runs on the original request.
criteria.yes: The item states that a pass-through reply leads atm to run the subcommand's normal or existing logic on the request as received (falls through, proceeds, continues, runs the unhooked path), or plans a test that the outcome equals the outcome with no hook registered.

addressed.instructions: `anchor.statement` requires that when a hook replies {"result": "pass-through"}, atm runs the subcommand's normal logic with the caller's original request, giving the same result as with no hook registered. Does `item.text` state this behaviour for that reply? Judge presence of this behaviour only, not whether something in the item conflicts with it.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item text conflicts with the directive, whether or not the directive is mentioned.
criteria.unclear: The item text is ambiguous enough that it might or might not conflict with the directive.
criteria.yes: The item text states a plan, approach, or decision that cannot be reconciled with the directive in the anchor statement.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` propose doing something that `anchor.statement` rules out, or propose a different approach than the one `anchor.statement` requires? Examples of contradiction: the anchor says to start from an existing implementation and the item plans a fresh implementation; the anchor forbids a dependency and the item adds it; the anchor fixes an order of work and the item reverses it. Silence about the directive is not a contradiction. Judge conflict only. For this anchor, examples of contradiction are: on a pass-through reply the item reports success without doing the work, changes the request before running it, bypasses part of the normal logic, or rejects the reply. Handling a refused, not-applicable or handled reply is not a contradiction.

results.statement: The hook runner must kill a hook still running at its timeout_ms deadline, at most 2500 ms for a task hook and 30000 ms for a cron tick or stop check, and fail the command with ATM_HOOK_TIMEOUT.
